chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Allie Ross's band: LeRoy Smith's men
summary: Zutty says Allie Ross's band grew from LeRoy Smith's band, a good band whose men doubled on many instruments, with a Puerto Rican bassist and three Puerto Rican violinists.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: But he wasn't going to take Zutty. They wanted me in Ally Ross' band.
Not then, that's what I say....
Ally Ross' band was built from LeRoy Smith's band.
Oh, they were the band that doubled on all kinds of instruments weren't they?
Yes, LeRoy Smith man. And (Geetmay?) the clarinet player he played old oboe and different other things.
And the whole band, they wanted Zutty.
LeRoy Smith, Tizol (Tessol?) he played on bass.
Tizol. He was a Puerto Rican.
And we had three violins, three Puerto Rican boys playing violin.
This was really rather an unhappy thing then?
Yes it was. It was a sad thing you know.
